newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER AFTER JULY JOBS DATA.
newsitem.headline: CANADA DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER AFTER JULY JOBS DATA.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker around C$1.3898 (US$0.7195)
from Thursday's close at C$1.3880 (US$0.7204) after the
release of disappointing Canadian jobs data * Overall
employment rose slightly in July, but a drop in full-time jobs
weighed on the currency * Canada unit seen trading between
C$1.3880 and C$1.3920 heading into next week.
Statistics Canada also reported that Canada's unemployment rate dipped to 9.0 percent in July, from 9.1 percent in June.
A Reuter survey of economists predicted employment would grow by 35,500 in July after an increase of 52,000 in June, and the unemployment would remain at 9.1 percent.

The jobs data diminished market expectations for a near-term interest rate hike by the Bank of Canada and hurt the Canadian dollar. "Neverthless, market participants have to be ready for a unilateral tightening from the (central bank) if the Canadian dollar drops in the low US$0.71 range," brokerage Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion Inc said in a report.
The Levesque report said the Bank of Canada will probably wait for Canada's second quarter gross domestic product figures before changing its monetary policy.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 82.40 Japanese yen from 85.23 yen on Thursday and dipped to 1.3268 marks from Thursday's 1.3452 marks.
